$note: Every rule id of CompilationRules, classed once. RuleParityTests.cs fails naming an id the file and the catalogue
do not share. 'depth' is where the compiler grades the rule: 'every' canvas the run enters, 'root' alone (with the
reason the run executes it as drawn below the root), 'document' for the stored text, or 'none' for a rule no
document raises; 'registration' for a catalogue-shape refusal. class 'editor': the editor grades it at the same depth,
and 'agreement' names the file both halves
grade it by. class 'compiler-only': 'why' says why the editor cannot know it from the document it holds. 'part'
names the half of an editor rule that is compiler-only. Decided by the two refusal rules: never refuse what the run
executes as drawn; refuse what it tolerates by doing nothing, or by doing what the author did not draw.

rules.why: Reads the canvas's wires. The run sorts every canvas it enters and fails on a cycle at any depth.
The run refuses a root without an entry node; a sub-canvas runs every node it holds in sort order, entry node or not, so there it runs as drawn.

The run refuses it at the root; in a sub-canvas the entry node is seeded, never run, so a bare wire into it only orders its source first, as drawn, and a mapping on it names an input the entry node lacks (wire-port-unknown).
The run refuses it at the root; a sub-canvas runs a node with no wire into it, as drawn.
The run refuses it at the root; a sub-canvas runs every node whether its entry node reaches it or not.
Reads the canvas's mappings. Two feeds into one input: the run applies the later and drops the other without a word, at any depth.
The fallback for a structure message the classifier does not know; every message the structure checks raise classifies to its own id, so no document produces it.

The editor's catalogue is the host's adapted view: createBlockCatalogueSource leaves out a type it cannot read, and a host may load it late, so a type absent there may be bound on the server, and refusing it would refuse what the compiler passes. Below such a node the editor skips what the compiler skips.
Reads the node's branches and its block's declared branch names, for a block the catalogue holds.
Reads the canvas's wires and node ids, and the root's outputMappings, which the editor's save writes back.
Reads the canvas's node ids.
Reads the node's required inputs, a branch's required outputs from its container's block, the workflow's required outputs, and what feeds each.
rules.part: The inputs a host resolver files for a node whose ports are resolved elsewhere are compiler-only: the resolver answers on the server.

rules.why: Reads the node's configuration and its block's required fields.

Reads each wire's mapping names against the ports of its two ends: a block's declared, dynamic and declared-output ports, the entry and exit nodes' canvas ports, passthrough names, and '_error' on a node whose policy is EmitError. The run finds nothing under a name its end lacks. Also reads the root's outputMappings against the workflow's declared outputs, as a wire into its exit node: the run writes any name one holds.
rules.part: An end whose ports a host resolver files (a block that runs a workflow), a port declared as a relation to an input nothing feeds (IterateOver's Item without a Collection), and a passthrough name the editor cannot trace to its end (through such a block, or a block its catalogue lacks) are compiler-only: the editor leaves such an end unchecked and counts every relation name, and every passthrough name it cannot trace, as a port. It traces the rest as the compiler does: a declared input, the last mapping into the name, then a configuration value. A key of a ContinueWithDefault node's defaultOutputJson that names no output is compiler-only too: the editor does not grade the key.

rules.why: Reads the node's declared outputs and its block's static outputs.

Port types come from the compiler's effective port model, which types a passthrough name only once it traces and takes a resolver's answer for a block that runs a workflow, compared under the host's widening table. The editor's type resolver is a second model; grading from it would refuse, or pass, where the two models differ.

A literal or configuration value is checked against the target's declared scalar type and text policy using the shared coercion vectors; a literal into a workflow output or an ordinary node is also measured on both halves by the rule-agreement file. A string beginning 'expr:' is an expression, graded by what it yields, never by its text.
rules.part: A literal into a passthrough name, into an input whose ports a host resolver files, or into an input whose declared term names a type parameter is graded by the compiler alone, against the term the binding pass gives it: the editor leaves such an end unchecked. So is a configuration value on a passthrough name, a ContinueWithDefault node's defaultOutputJson value, and the format of a DateTime or Uuid literal, which the editor reads as a JSON string only. A host type that declares no literal form refuses every literal on both halves. Body-exit `Sources` raw keys projected from a declared branch output are also compiler-only: .NET grades them against the projected port type, while the editor does not grade those raw keys.

rules.why: Reads each stored type name with the grammar both halves share.
Reads the key of each stored Map type with the grammar both halves share.
The one reader refuses the stored text; the editor reads it with the same rules (storedDocument.ts).
An exception in the compiler or in host code it called: a fault, not a property of the document.
A passthrough port gets its term from its feed, and a literal of null, [] or an array without an element least upper bound gives none; the editor holds no effective types.

The vocabulary is the host's compile table (its declared and widened names and its aliases). The editor holds a registry for authoring and keeps a name it does not register through load (normalize passes it unchanged), so it cannot grade a stored name against the table the compile uses.

The vocabulary is the host's compile table (its declared and widened names and its aliases). The editor holds a registry for authoring and keeps a name it does not register through load (normalize passes it unchanged), so it cannot grade a stored name against the table the compile uses.

A node's type parameter is bound from the terms its sites carry: wires, expressions, literals and typeArguments. Two exact bindings that differ, or lower bounds with no least upper bound, are found only from those terms, and the editor holds no effective types.

A site needs a type parameter that no site of the node binds: a literal such as [] or null on a port whose term names it, or a read of a port whose term names it. Whether anything binds it is known only from the terms the binding pass gives, which the editor does not hold.
A type parameter's binding is graded against the capabilities the block declares for it; the binding is the binding pass's, which the editor does not hold.

rules.part: Every declaration rule but the parse check is compiler-only: the server refuses an undeclared or repeated type parameter, an unknown capability, a body-bound parameter on an input, Json off an output or a misplaced Expression<T> when it reads its catalogue, and the editor's catalogue reader does not grade them.
rules.why: A declared term (a port type or a scope variable type) that does not parse under the declaration grammar is refused when the host catalogue is read. The declaration belongs to the catalogue, not the stored document.
The expression language belongs to whoever evaluates it (docs/faq.md): the library's editor owns the expr: protocol only, and a host plugs its own editor into renderExpressionEditor.
Needs the expression language (see expression-syntax) and the compiler's scope, its sort order and port model.
The compiler recognizes the library namespaces and host registrations; an unregistered namespace has no resolver and is refused.

Needs the expression language and the declared type of the value a member or index is read out of: the port model, a parameter's type or a host check's answer. No term allows a member or an index: a scalar, a collection (read whole), a Json value (opaque, read only through a projection) and a type with no stated shape are refused.
Needs the expression typer: the terms of the operands, the overloads of expression-functions.json and the vocabulary's least upper bound, none of which the editor evaluates.
Needs the expression typer's result term and the effective term of its target, which the binding pass gives a port: the editor types no expression and binds no parameter.

The stored-document reader refuses a key absent from the grammar at any listed object position, in a definition or a parameter list; the editor reads both through the same grammar and reports the same code.
The stored-document reader refuses two connections with one id; the editor reads the same rules and reports the same code.
The stored-document reader refuses a stored outputMappings key; the editor reads the same rules and reports the same code.
The one reader refuses a stored parameter list; the editor reads it with the same rules (readParameterListText).
Reads the reference input a block names (runsWorkflowFrom), its configured value and the mappings into it.
rules.part: A configured reference no host resolver answered for is compiler-only: the resolver answers on the server.

rules.why: Reads the mappings into the reference input a block names (runsWorkflowFrom).
Reads the block's SecretValues declaration, which the editor's adapted catalogue view carries only for the blocks it could read; the run would copy the stored forms into the outputs.
Reads the block's SecretValues declaration, which the editor's adapted catalogue view carries only for the blocks it could read; the key/value rows refuse such a key, and the run would refuse it too.
Reads the node's resilience configuration values.
Reads the node's configuration keys.
Reads the node's error policy.

Only the compile grades an errorPolicy on an entry or exit node, whatever the policy: the editor offers no policy control on such a node and does not grade one it is handed. A configuration key errorPolicy on such a node stays error-policy-in-configuration.
The stored-document grammar refuses authored dotted names and the compiler checks host-resolved ports that the reader cannot see.

The bound is the library's own model's, not the document's: a node id is text the editor holds, but the width it has to fit is automation.execution_node_log's NodeId column, and the editor holds no schema — a host may map its own, wider one. Graded by the compiler, which is the gate every publish and every admission passes; the editor's own node ids are what createId writes.

The same table and the same width, and the id is the host's registry's rather than the document's: the editor's catalogue is the host's adapted view (see block-type-unknown), so a type absent there may be bound on the server with an id the editor never sees.
The editor and compiler refuse repeated wires with the same source and target; the store prevents authoring them.
Reads the node's InputPorts and OutputPorts configuration and whether its block has dynamic ports.
Reads the node's declared outputs and whether its block supports declared outputs.
Reads the keys of a declared output's sources and the sub-canvas names of its block.
The editor has no compiler vocabulary or resolver answers to decide whether this type term contains Json.
A projection is checked against its source's and its target's effective terms after binding, which only the compiler holds; the editor never grades binding or assignability between wires.
A stored typeArguments key must name a parameter declared by the node block.
